scenes.title: Surprise and Probability
scenes.visual: A large text label 'Surprise = log2(1 / P)' sits at the top center. Below it, two boxes appear side by side: the left box shows 'Heads (P = 0.5)' and 'Surprise = 1 bit', while the right box shows 'Rare Event (P = 0.125)' and 'Surprise = 3 bits'. An arrow points from the low probability to high surprise.
scenes.narration: In information theory, surprise measures how unexpected an event is. A rare outcome carries much more information, or surprise, than a common one.

scenes.title: Fair Coin Entropy
scenes.visual: At the top center, the formula 'H = - sum(P * log2(P))' is displayed. Below it, two columns appear for a fair coin: 'Heads: P=0.5, Surprise=1 bit' and 'Tails: P=0.5, Surprise=1 bit'. A weighted sum calculation animates below, yielding 'Average Surprise (Entropy) = 1.0 bit'.
scenes.narration: Entropy is simply the average surprise across all possible outcomes. For a fair coin, both heads and tails give one bit of surprise, so the average entropy is exactly one bit.

scenes.title: Biased Coin Entropy
scenes.visual: The top formula remains. The columns update for a 90% biased coin: 'Heads: P=0.9, Surprise=0.15 bits' and 'Tails: P=0.1, Surprise=3.32 bits'. The weighted average animates: '0.9*(0.15) + 0.1*(3.32)', resulting in 'Entropy = 0.47 bits', highlighted with a green box.
scenes.narration: If a coin is heavily biased, you usually get heads with almost no surprise, and rarely get tails. Weighing these together gives a much lower average surprise of just 0.47 bits.

scenes.title: Entropy Curve
scenes.visual: A 2D coordinate system appears with the x-axis labeled 'Probability of Heads (p)' from 0 to 1, and the y-axis labeled 'Entropy H(p)' from 0 to 1. A smooth parabolic curve plots from (0,0), reaching a peak at (0.5, 1.0), and falling back to (1,0). A dot moves along the curve to highlight the maximum at p=0.5.
scenes.narration: Plotting entropy against probability reveals that uncertainty peaks when outcomes are equally likely. When the result is completely predictable, entropy drops to zero.
